paragraphs: Ecopia AI uses artificial intelligence to convert high-resolution geospatial imagery into accurate, up-to-date vector maps for data-driven decision-making. For municipal and state government the data is offered for transportation networks, public safety and stormwater planning. Off-the-shelf offerings sit alongside customized global feature extraction.

Its 3D Land Cover product delivers planimetric vector layers for buildings, roads, driveways, sidewalks, water bodies, sports fields and overlapping tree canopy, with height attribution for buildings. The company states that features are extracted from high-resolution imagery with greater than 95% geometric accuracy. Partner imagery providers capture fresh imagery every year, which lets the company detect change and deliver annual updates. A separate transportation product covers sidewalks, crosswalks, medians, bike lanes, turning lanes, paint striping and intersections. Those layers carry attributes such as width, material and feature type, distinguishing a left turn lane from a right turn lane.

The transportation data is aimed at AEC firms, MPOs and DOTs. Stated uses include assessing sidewalk width and curb characteristics against ADA regulations. Another stated use is emergency services and dispatch planning, drawing on 3D maps of buildings, roads and driveways. Ecopia says it produces millions of square kilometers of vector data per month. It also announced a self-serve platform for high-precision geospatial data downloads.
